translations.text: And he called Moses on the seventh day from within the cloud, and he saw the glory of the Lord like a fire burning on the mountain’s summit.

And you, write down for yourself all the words that I make known to you today, for I know their rebelliousness and their stiff necks even before I bring them into the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘To your descendants I will give a land flowing with milk and honey.’
They will make high places, groves, and carved images for themselves, and each will bow down to his own idol. They will sacrifice their children to demons and to every work of their hearts’ error.
And after this they will return to me in complete uprightness, with all their heart and all their soul.
Then we saw his work, blessed him, and praised him in his presence for all his work, for he made seven great works on the first day.
And it separates light from darkness, providing well-being so that everything that sprouts and grows on the earth may flourish.
And it was granted to this one that all its days should be blessed and holy.
He created heaven and earth and everything that was created in six days.
And Adam named them all, each with its own name, and whatever he called them became their name.
During these five days Adam watched all these, male and female, among every kind on earth. But he was alone, and no helper like himself was found for him.
And he awakened Adam from his sleep.
For this reason a man and a woman shall be one, and for this reason he shall leave his father and mother and join himself to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
In the first week: Adam and his rib, his wife; and in the second week he showed her to him.
After Adam had completed forty days in the land where he was created, we brought him into the Garden of Eden to cultivate it and guard it.

For this reason a commandment was written on the heavenly tablets concerning a woman who gives birth: if she gives birth to a male, she shall remain in her impurity for seven days, corresponding to the first seven days. For thirty-three days she shall remain in the blood of purification. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until she completes these days prescribed for a male child.
And the woman saw that the tree was pleasant and pleasing to the eye, and that its fruit was good to eat.

He was the first to write a testimony and to testify to humanity throughout the generations of the earth. He recounted the weeks of the jubilees, made known the days of the years, arranged the months, and recounted the sabbatical years, as we had made them known to him. 19 And he saw what had happened and what would happen in a vision during his sleep—what would happen to humanity throughout their generations until the day of judgment. He saw and understood everything.

And wickedness increased on the earth, and all flesh corrupted its way, from humans to livestock, wild animals, birds, and everything that moves on the earth. They all corrupted their ways and their order.
And there is nothing in heaven or on earth, in light or in darkness, in Sheol or in the deep.
And he entered in his sixth [?], in the second month. From the beginning of the second month until the sixteenth day, he and everything that we brought to him entered the ark.
And the waters increased on the earth. The waters rose fifteen cubits above every high mountain, and the ark was lifted above the earth and moved over the surface of the waters.
And he placed fat on the altar and took an ox, a [?], a sheep, kids, salt, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.

And the Lord smelled the pleasing fragrance and made a covenant with him that there would be no floodwaters to destroy the earth. Throughout all the days of the earth, sowing and harvest shall not cease. Cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not change their order or cease forever.
And you, grow and multiply on the earth, increase upon it, and be a blessing amid the fear and dread of you.

And look, I have given you all wild animals, all livestock, everything that flies, everything that moves on the earth, and the fish in the waters—everything for food. As with the green grass, I have given you everything to eat.

But do not eat flesh with its spirit, with its blood, for the life of every living creature is in its blood, so that your blood may not be required for your lives. From the hand of every person, from the hand of everyone, I will require human blood.
Thus it was engraved and ordained on the heavenly tablets.
He first made atonement and placed some of its blood on the flesh of the sacrifice he had made. He offered up all the fat on the altar where he had made a burnt offering, an ox, a goat, and sheep.

In the twenty-eighth jubilee, Noah began to instruct his grandchildren in the ordinances and commandments, all the judgments he knew. He charged his children to practice righteousness, to cover the nakedness of their bodies, to bless the one who created them, to honor father and mother, to love one another, and to keep themselves from sexual immorality, impurity, and all wrongdoing.

For because of these three things the flood came upon the earth: because of the sexual immorality committed by the Watchers, contrary to the command governing them, in pursuing the daughters of men. They took wives for themselves from all those they chose and brought about the beginning of impurity. 22 And they fathered children, the Nephilim, and they were all unlike one another.
For everyone who sheds human blood and everyone who eats the blood of any living creature will all be wiped out from the earth.
The son grew up, and his father taught him writing. He went to seek a place for himself where he could establish a city.

He knew that a blessed share and a blessing had fallen to Shem and his descendants for all generations forever: all the land of Edom, all the land of the Red Sea, all the land of the east, India, the land by the Red Sea and its mountains, all the land of Bashan, all the land of Lebanon, and the islands of Caphtor.
The second share fell to Ham, beyond the Gihon toward the north, to the right of the garden. It runs toward the north and passes through all the mountains of fire.

It reaches southward to the end of Gadir and reaches the shore of the sea, into the waters of the Great Sea, until it approaches the river Gihon. It follows the river Gihon until it approaches the right side of the garden of Edom.
This is the land that fell to Ham as his share, which he and his descendants were to possess forever, throughout their generations, forever.

The third share fell to Japheth, beyond the river Tina, south of the outlet of its waters. It runs toward the southeast, through the whole region of Gog and all the regions east of them. 26 It runs farther southward and goes toward the mountains of Kelt to the south and toward the Sea of Ma'uk. It reaches east of Gadir, as far as the edge of the waters of the sea.

The third share fell to Arphaxad: all the land of the region of the Chaldeans east of the Euphrates, near the Red Sea, and all the waters of the wilderness as far as the vicinity of the gulf facing Egypt; all the land of Lebanon, Senir, and Amana, as far as the vicinity of the Euphrates.
The seventh share fell to Tiras: four large islands in the middle of the sea, near Ham's share.
Thus Noah's sons divided the land among their children in the presence of Noah their father.

They all said, “Let it be so, and let it be so for them and their descendants forever, throughout their generations, until the day of judgment, when the Lord God will judge them with sword and fire for all the evil impurity of their transgressions, with which they filled the earth with guilt, impurity, sexual immorality, and sin.”
In the third week of this jubilee, unclean demons began to lead the children of Noah's sons astray, to drive them mad, and to destroy them.
Noah's sons came to Noah their father and told him about the demons that were leading his grandchildren astray, driving them mad, and killing them.

He prayed before the Lord his God and said, “God of the spirits in all living creatures, you have shown me mercy and saved me and my children from the waters of the flood. You did not cause me to perish as you did the children of destruction, for your kindness toward me is great, and your mercy toward my life is abundant.”
Our God told us to bind them all.
Who lived longer on the earth than any other human being, except Enoch, because of his righteousness, in which he was perfect.

In the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week, in its first year, Reu took a wife named Ara, the daughter of Ur son of Chesed. She bore him a son, and he named him Serug, in the seventh week [?] of this week.

Ud son of Chesed built the city of Araha of the Chaldeans and named it after himself and his father. 4 They made cast images for themselves, and each person bowed down to the idol he had cast for himself.
Worship the God of heaven, who sends down rain.

Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them? They are the work of human hands, and you carry them on your shoulders. You gain no help from them, only great disgrace for those who make them and delusion of heart for those who worship them. Do not worship them. 6 He said to him, “I know this too, my son. What should I do about the people who have ordered me to serve before them? 7 If I tell them the truth, they will kill me, because their souls cling to these things, to worship and praise them.”
He told this to his two brothers, and they became angry with him, so he kept silent.
In the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in its seventh year, Abram took a wife named Sarai, his father's daughter, and she became his wife.
His brother Haran took a wife in the third year of the third week. She bore him a son in the seventh year of this week, and he named him Lot.
Haran hurried to save them, but the fire blazed over him, and he was burned in the fire. He died in Ur of the Chaldeans before his father Terah, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldeans.
If he wishes, he makes it rain morning and evening; and if he wishes, he does not send it down. Everything is in his hands.

He prayed that night and said, “My God, my God, God Most High, you alone are my God. You created everything, and everything came into being and exists through the work of your hands. I have chosen you and your divinity.”
The Lord said to him, “I will give this land to you and your descendants.” 4 He built an altar there and offered incense on it to the Lord, who had appeared to him.
When Pharaoh took Sarai, Abram's wife, the Lord struck Pharaoh and his household with a great plague because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
Abram said to him, “I raise my hands to God Most High: I will not take anything that belongs to you, from a thread to a sandal strap, so that you cannot say, ‘I made Abram rich.’”
The Lord said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you shall no longer call her Sarai, for her name is Sarah.”

Now I tell you that the children of Israel will prove false to this ordinance and will not circumcise their children according to this entire law. They will leave some of the flesh of their circumcision when circumcising their children, and all the children of Beliar will leave their children uncircumcised, just as they were born.
Likewise, the Lord will bring judgment upon places [?] where they act as Sodom did, according to the judgment upon Sodom.
He celebrated this festival for seven days, rejoicing with all his heart and all his soul, he and everyone in his household. There was no stranger with him, nor anyone who was uncircumcised.

For this reason it was ordained on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel that they should celebrate the Festival of Booths with joy for seven days in the seventh month, as something acceptable before the Lord—an eternal law throughout their generations, every year.

There is no limit of days for this, for it is ordained forever for Israel that they should celebrate it and live in booths, place wreaths on their heads, and take leafy branches and willows from the stream.
Abraham took palm shoots and fruit from good trees. Each day he went around the altar with the branches seven times a day. In the morning he praised and glorified his God for everything, with joy.
In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee, Isaac was weaned. Abraham held a great feast in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.

And Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian woman, [?] before his father Abraham in that place. Abraham rejoiced and blessed the Lord because he had seen offspring of his own and had not died without children. 3 And he remembered the words that he had spoken on the day when Lot separated from him.
He built an altar and placed wood on it. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the wood above the altar. He stretched out his hand to take the knife to slaughter his son Isaac.

This was the tenth trial with which Abraham was tested, and he was found faithful and patient in spirit. 9 He said nothing concerning the promise about the land that the Lord had said he would give to him and to his descendants after him.

He said to her, “My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, for he will take my place on earth and be a blessing among humankind and a source of pride for all the descendants of Shem. 18 For I know that the Lord will choose him for himself as a people set apart from all those on the face of the earth.”
“Keep this commandment and carry it out, my son, so that you may act rightly in everything you do.”
“Be careful not to follow their ways or walk in their footsteps, and do not commit a sin leading to death before God Most High.”
He offered a peace offering and held a joyful feast in the presence of his brother Ishmael.

“And you, my son Jacob, may God Most High help you, and may the God of heaven bless you and keep you away from their impurity and all their wrongdoing. 20 Be careful, my son Jacob, not to take a wife from any of the descendants of the daughters of Canaan.”

He lived for three jubilees and four weeks of years, a hundred and seventy-five years, and completed the days of his life, old and full of years. 9 For the lifetimes of the earliest people were nineteen jubilees.

In those days, if a man lives for a jubilee and a half, they will say of him, “He has lived a long time.” Most of his days will be pain, toil, and distress, and there will be no peace. 13 For there will be plague upon plague, wound upon wound, distress upon distress, bad news upon bad news, illness upon illness, and every similar evil punishment, one along with another: illness, upheaval, snow, hail, frost, fever, chills, numbness, famine, death, the sword, and captivity.
Then they will say of the people of earlier times, “Their days were long, as much as a thousand years, and good.”

They will rise up with swords and slaughter to bring them back to the way, but they will not return until they have shed much blood on the earth, fighting one another. 21 Those who survive will not turn from their wickedness to the way of righteousness, for they will all rise up for deceit and wealth, so that each may take everything belonging to his neighbor. They will call themselves by a great name, but not in truth or righteousness, and they will defile the holy of holies with the impurity of their corrupt abominations.
A great plague from the Lord will come upon the deeds of that generation, and he will hand them over to the sword, judgment, captivity, plunder, and destruction.
Their bones will rest in the earth.
“And you, Moses, write down these words, for this is how they are written, and they will be entered as testimony on the heavenly tablets for the generations forever.”

After Abraham died, the Lord blessed his son Isaac. He left Hebron and went to live by the Well of the Vision for seven years, beginning in the first year of the third week of this jubilee. 2 In the year of the fourth week, a famine began in the land, apart from the earlier famine that had occurred in Abraham’s days.
Jacob cooked a lentil stew, and Esau came from the field hungry. He said to his brother Jacob, “Give me some of this wheat stew.”
Esau said to himself, “I am going to die. What use is being the firstborn?” He said to Jacob, “I give it to you.”
There was a famine in the land, and Isaac set out to go down to Egypt in the second year of this week. He went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, at Gerar.

He called that place the Well of the Oath, because there he swore an oath to Abimelech, to Ahuzzath his deputy, and to Phicol, commander of his guard. 27 Isaac realized that day that he had sworn to make peace with them under compulsion.
On that day Isaac cursed the Philistines and said, “May the Philistines be cursed among all the nations for the day of wrath and anger.”

“For even if he ascends to heaven, he will be brought down from there. Even if he establishes himself firmly in the earth, he will be torn out from there. Even if he hides among the nations, he will be uprooted from there. And even if he descends into Sheol, his punishment will increase there.”

Then Jacob spoke with Rebekah his mother and said to her, “Look, Mother, I am now nine weeks of years old. I have known no woman, nor have I touched one or become betrothed. Nor do I intend to take a wife for myself from any of the descendants of the daughters of Canaan. 5 For I remember, Mother, the words of Abraham our father, and what he commanded me: not to take a wife from any of the descendants of the house of Canaan, but to take a wife for myself from the descendants of my father’s house and from my relatives. 6 I heard some time ago, Mother, that daughters had been born to Laban your brother, and I have set my heart on taking a wife from among them.”

“For this reason I have guarded myself in spirit, so that I might not sin or corrupt myself in any of my ways throughout my life. For our father Abraham gave me many commands concerning marriage and sexual immorality, along with everything else he commanded me. 8 For these twenty-two years my brother has argued with me, repeatedly saying to me, ‘My brother, take as your wife a sister of my two wives.’ But I am unwilling to do as he has done.”

“I swear before you, Mother, that throughout my life I will not take a wife for myself from any of the descendants of the daughters of Canaan, nor will I act wickedly as my brother has done. 10 Do not be afraid, Mother. Be assured that I will do your will, walk uprightly, and never corrupt my ways.”

Then she lifted her face toward heaven, spread out the fingers of her hands, opened her mouth, and blessed the Most High God, who created heaven and earth. She gave him thanks and praise. 12 She said, “Blessed be the Lord God, and blessed be his name forever and ever.”

“Bless him, Lord, and place a righteous blessing in my mouth, so that I may bless him.” 14 At that moment a spirit of righteousness descended into her mouth. She placed both her hands on Jacob’s head and said:

“Just as you have given rest to your mother’s spirit during her [?], may the womb of the woman who bore you and my compassion likewise bless you. May my breasts bless you, and may my mouth and tongue praise you. Multiply, 20 grow great, and spread throughout the earth. May your descendants be complete throughout all the world, amid the joy of heaven and earth.”
Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to Esau.
Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Mother, I will not withhold anything that my father would eat and enjoy. But I am afraid, Mother, that he may recognize my voice and want to feel me.”
He went in to his father and said, “I am your son. I have done as you told me. Get up, sit down, and eat some of what I have hunted, Father, so that your soul may bless me.”
Isaac said to him, “Come near, my son, so that I may feel you and determine whether you are my son Esau or not.”

He said, “Are you my son Esau?” He answered, “I am your son.” Then he said, “Bring it to me, and let me eat some of what you have hunted, my son, so that my soul may bless.” 20 He brought it to him, and he ate. [?] wine for him, and he drank.
He smelled the scent and fragrance of his clothes, blessed him, and said, “Look, the scent of my son is like the scent of a field that the Lord has blessed.”
“May the Lord give to you and increase your share of the dew of heaven and the dew of the earth. May he multiply abundant wheat and oil for you.”

“Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother’s children bow down to you. May all the blessings with which the Lord blessed me and blessed Abraham my father belong to you and your descendants forever. Cursed be whoever curses you, and blessed be whoever blesses you.”
After Isaac finished blessing his son Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from Isaac his father, he hid himself.
He too prepared food and brought it to his father.
Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He said to him, “I am Esau, your firstborn, your son. I have done as you commanded me.”

Isaac was extremely astonished and said, “Who was it who went out, hunted game for me, and brought it? I ate some of everything before you came, and I blessed him. May he be blessed, together with all his descendants, forever.”
When Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried out very loudly and bitterly and said to his father, “Bless me too, Father!”
He said to him, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessings.”
Jacob again went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore him a third son. He named him Levi.
When Rachel saw that Leah had borne Jacob four sons—Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah—
He went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a son.
Jacob again went in to Bilhah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a second son. Rachel named him Naphtali, on the fifth day of the seventh month, in the second year of the fourth week of years.

When Leah saw that she had become barren and was no longer bearing children, she too became jealous of Rachel. She too gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife. She conceived and bore a son, and Leah named him Gad, on the twelfth day of the eighth month, in the third year of the fourth week of years.
He again went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a second son. Leah named him Asher, on the second day of the eleventh month, in the fifth year of the fourth week of years.
Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a son. He named him Issachar, on the fourth day of the fifth month, in the fourth year of the fourth week of years.
Jacob went in to her a second time, and she conceived and bore two children, a son and a daughter. She named the son Zebulun and the daughter Dinah.
God had mercy on Rachel and opened her womb.

In the days when Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wives and my children, so that I may go to my father Isaac and establish a household for myself. For I have completed the years during which I served you in exchange for your two daughters, and I will go to my father’s house.”
Laban said to Jacob, “Stay with me for wages, and tend my flocks for me again, and take your wages.”
Jacob blessed the God of his father Isaac and the God of Abraham, his father’s father.
Jacob sent Laban away, and he went to Mesopotamia, the land of the east.
He crossed the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the tenth and [?] day.

In the first year of the fifth week of years in this jubilee, he crossed the Jordan and settled beyond the Jordan. He pastured his sheep from the Sea of the Heap as far as Beth-shan, as far as Dothan, and as far as [?] Akrabbim.
From all his possessions he would send his father Isaac clothing and food, meat and drink, milk and butter, milk cakes, and dates from the lowlands.

He also sent these to his mother Rebekah four times a year, at the intervals of the months: between plowing and harvesting, between spring and the rainy season, and between winter and summer, at Abraham’s dwelling.
For Isaac had returned from the Well of the Oath and gone up to the dwelling of his father Abraham. He lived there, away from his son Esau.
From there Jacob would send his father and mother everything he sent them, from time to time, for all their needs.
1. After Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Laban went to shear his sheep, for they were far away from him, a three-day journey.
There they abducted Dinah, Jacob’s daughter, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of the land. He slept with her and defiled her.
He begged her father to give her to him as a wife, and he also asked her brothers for her as his wife.

Simeon and Levi entered Shechem unexpectedly and carried out judgment on all the men of Shechem. They killed every man they found in it and did not leave even one alive. They killed them all cruelly because they had defiled Dinah, their sister.
Let no sexual immorality or uncleanness be found in Israel throughout all the days of the generations of the earth, for Israel is holy to the Lord.
For it is punishment upon punishment and curse upon curse, and every judgment, punishment, and curse will come.
The descendants of Levi were chosen for the priesthood and as Levites, to serve before the Lord as we do at all times.
In this way they will record blessing and righteousness for him as a testimony on the heavenly tablets, before the God of all.

We remember the righteousness that a person practiced during his lifetime, at every season of the year. They will record it for a thousand generations, and it will come to him and to his descendants after him. He will be recorded as a friend and a righteous person on the heavenly tablets.

I have written all these things for you and commanded you to tell the children of Israel not to commit sin, transgress the ordinance, or break the covenant established for them to observe, so that they may be recorded as friends. 22 But if they transgress and follow any of the ways of uncleanness, they will be recorded on the heavenly tablets as enemies. They will be erased from the book of the living and recorded in the book of those who perish, among those who are uprooted from the earth.

On the day when Jacob's sons killed the people of Shechem, a written record was brought up to heaven for them, stating that they had acted righteously and justly and taken vengeance on sinners. It was recorded as a blessing.
Jacob went to his father Isaac, into his room where he lay.
He turned and kissed him again and embraced him. He rejoiced greatly because he had seen the children of Jacob, his righteous son.
He came out from between his feet, fell down, and bowed to him, and he blessed them.

He said, “Now I know that I and my children have an everlasting hope before the God of all.” Thus it was ordained concerning both of them, and they will record it for them as an everlasting testimony on the heavenly tablets, just as Isaac blessed them.

On the [?] and fifth day of this month, he brought to the altar fourteen bulls from the cattle, twenty-eight rams, forty-nine sheep, sixty lambs, and twenty-nine young goats, as a burnt offering on the altar and an acceptable offering, a pleasing fragrance before God.
When the fire consumed it, he burned frankincense above it on the fire.
For grain is to be eaten in its year, until the time of the year's grain harvest; wine until the time of the grape harvest; and oil until the time of its season.

He said to him again, “I am the Lord who created heaven and earth. I will make you grow and multiply you exceedingly. Kings will come from you, and they will rule everywhere that human footsteps tread.”

He saw in a vision at night, and there was an angel descending from heaven with seven tablets in his hands. He gave them to Jacob, and Jacob read them. He read everything written in them that would happen to him and his children throughout all ages.
He showed him everything written on the tablets and said to him, “Do not build up this place or make it an everlasting sanctuary, and do not settle here, for this is not the place.”
For you will die peacefully in Egypt, and in this land you will be buried with honor in the tomb of your fathers, with Abraham and Isaac.
Do not be afraid, for everything will happen just as you have seen and read. You too must write down everything just as you have seen and read it.
Jacob said, “Lord, how will I remember everything that I have read and seen?”

On the night of the twenty-third day of this month, Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died. They buried her below the city, beneath the oak by the river. He called that place Deborah's River, and its oak the Oak of Deborah's Mourning.
He followed his mother until he approached the land of Kabratan, and he stayed there.
Jacob was very angry with Reuben because he had slept with Bilhah, for he had uncovered his father's nakedness.

And you, Moses, command the children of Israel to observe this command, for it carries a sentence of death and is an impurity. There is no forgiveness or atonement forever for a man who does this, except to put him to death, kill him, stone him with stones, and uproot him from among the people of our God.
And they went and bowed down before Isaac and Rebekah.
And in the sixth year of this week of years, in the forty-fourth jubilee.
And all seven kings of the Amorites gathered against them to kill them, hiding beneath the trees, and to plunder their livestock.

And Jacob, Levi, Judah, and Joseph were in the house with Isaac their father, for his spirit was sorrowful, and they could not leave him. Benjamin was the youngest, and for this reason he stayed with him.

And the kings of Tappuah, the kings of Aresa, the kings of Seragan, the kings of Shiloh, the king of Gaash, the king of Beth-horon, and the king of Maannisakir came, along with all those who lived in these hills, who lived in the wooded land of Canaan.

And on that day Bilhah heard that Joseph had perished, and she died while mourning him. She had been living in Qafr​​atef. Dinah his daughter also died after Joseph had perished. These three sorrows came upon Israel in one month. 16 And they buried Bilhah opposite Rachel’s tomb, and they buried Dinah his daughter there also.

And Jacob said to her, “I would be blessed, Mother, if my days approached the length of your life and my strength remained with me as yours does. You will not die, for you speak to me about your death in vain and to no purpose.”
And Isaac said to her, “I too know and see how Jacob acts toward us, that he honors us with all his heart.”

And Rebekah sent and summoned Esau, and he came to her. She said to him, “My son, I have a request to make of you. Say that you will do it, my son.” 19 And he said, “I will do everything you tell me, and I will not refuse your request.”

And she said to him, “I ask you, on the day when I die, to bring me in and bury me near Sarah, your father’s mother, and that you and Jacob love one another. Let neither seek harm against his brother, but love one another, so that you may prosper, my sons, and be honored in the land. Let no enemy rejoice over you, and may you be a blessing and receive mercy in the eyes of all who love you.”
And he said, “I will do everything you tell me, and on the day of your death I will bury you near Sarah, my father’s mother, just as you have desired that her bones should be near your bones.”
“And I love Jacob my brother more than all other flesh, and I have no brother in all the earth except him alone.”
“And I likewise beg you to admonish Jacob concerning me and my children, for I know that he will surely reign over me and over my children.”
And she summoned Jacob in Esau’s presence and commanded him according to the words she had spoken with Esau.
“And this I command you, my sons: practice righteousness and justice on the earth, so that the Lord may bring upon you everything that the Lord said he would do for Abraham and his descendants.”
And Jacob lived in the hills of Hebron, in the tower in the land where his father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.

And Leah his wife died in the fourth year of the second week of years of the forty-fifth jubilee. He buried her in the double cave, near Rebekah his mother, to the left of the tomb of Sarah, his father’s mother. 22 And all her children and his children came to mourn Leah his wife with him and to comfort him concerning her, for he was mourning her. 23 For he had loved her very deeply since Rachel her sister died, because she was blameless and upright in all her ways and honored Jacob.
And he remembered all the deeds she had done during her life, and he mourned her greatly, for he loved her with all his heart and with all his soul.
And on the day when Isaac, the father of Jacob and Esau, died, Esau’s sons heard that Isaac had given the rights of the firstborn to Jacob his younger son.
And they quarreled with their father, saying, “Why, when you are the elder and Jacob is younger, did your father give him the rights of the firstborn and pass you over?”
They sent to Aram and to Adoram, their father's friend, and hired a thousand chosen warriors and fighting men to accompany them.

The people of Hebron sent word to him, saying, “Look, your brother has come against you to fight you with four thousand men armed with swords and carrying shields and weapons of war.” They told him because they loved Jacob more than Esau, for Jacob was a more gracious and merciful man than Esau.
They sent to their father to ask whether they should make peace with them or kill them.

Jacob sent word to his sons to make peace. They made peace with them and imposed the yoke of tribute on them, requiring them to pay tribute to Jacob and all his sons. 13 They continued paying tribute to Jacob until the day Jacob went down to Egypt.
The descendants of Edom have not thrown off the yoke of tribute that the twelve sons of Jacob imposed on them, to this day.
These are the kings who reigned in Edom before a king reigned over the descendants of Israel, to this day, in the land of Edom.
Balak son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
Balak died, and Jobab son of Zerah, from Bozrah, reigned in his place.
Jacob lived in the land where his father had lived as a foreigner, the land of Canaan. 2 These are the descendants of Jacob.
When the woman saw that he would not sleep with her, she accused him before his master, saying, “Your Hebrew servant, whom you love, wanted to force me to sleep with him.”
The Egyptian saw Joseph's garment and the broken door.
Then the chief cupbearer remembered Joseph and told the king about him. They brought him out of prison, and the king recounted both his dreams before him.
God gave Joseph favor and mercy in Pharaoh's eyes. Pharaoh said to his servants, “We cannot find a man as wise and understanding as this man, for the Spirit of God is with him.”
He clothed him in fine linen and placed a gold chain around his neck.
Joseph ruled over the whole land of Egypt. All Pharaoh's officials, all his servants, and everyone who performed the king's work loved him.

The land of Egypt was at peace before Pharaoh because of Joseph, for God was with him and gave him favor and mercy above all his relatives, before everyone who knew him and those who heard reports about him. Pharaoh's kingdom was well established, and there was no adversary and no evil.
The king gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah.
On the day Joseph stood before Pharaoh, he was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh.

In that year Isaac died. What Joseph had said concerning the interpretation of the two dreams came to pass just as he had told him. There were seven years of abundance throughout the land of Egypt, and the land produced plentifully: one measure yielded eighteen hundred measures.
Joseph gathered food in each city for that city, until they were filled with grain, so much that they could no longer count or measure it because of its abundance.
Onan knew that the offspring would not be his but his brother's.
Judah went to his sheep, and she went to her father's house.
We told Judah that neither of his two sons had slept with her.

They went up from the land of Egypt and reached the land of Canaan. They told their father everything that had happened to them, how the ruler of the land had spoken harshly to them, and how he had detained Simeon until they brought Benjamin to him.
The famine increased and grew severe in the land of Canaan and in every land except the land of Egypt.
And he supplied the people of Egypt with food in the first year of the famine.

And he sent him with them in the second year of this week of years, at the new moon. They reached the land of Egypt with all those who were traveling, and he put gifts into their hands: storax resin, almonds, terebinth nuts, and pure honey.

And Joseph said to them, “I fear God. As for you, go to your homes, but let your brother remain a slave, because you have done wrong. Do you not know that a man practices divination with his cup, as I do with this cup? Yet you stole it from me.”
And Joseph saw that all their hearts were united with one another for good. He could no longer restrain himself and told them that he was Joseph.
And Jacob remembered the dream he had seen at Bethel and was afraid to go down to Egypt. 3 And he was considering sending word to Joseph to come to him, so that he himself would not have to go down.
And Israel sent his son Judah ahead of him to his son Joseph to inspect the land of Goshen, because Joseph had told his brothers to come and settle there, so that they would be near him.
Levi and his sons—and these are the names of his sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari—four in all.
And before his father entered Egypt, sons were born to Joseph in Egypt, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of Heliopolis, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim.
And Ew, who was born after the year of famine, died in Egypt.
And Joseph came to meet his father Jacob in the land of Goshen. He embraced his father's neck and wept.
And Israel lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years.

And he rested with his ancestors and was buried in the cave of Machpelah in the land of Canaan, near his father Abraham, in the grave he had dug for himself in the cave of Machpelah in the land of Hebron.
And he gave all his books and the books of his ancestors to his son Levi, so that he would preserve them and make new copies of them for his children, down to this day.

And after Jacob died, the children of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt and became a numerous people. They were all united in their hearts, so that each brother loved his brothers and each man helped his brother. They multiplied and increased greatly.
And there was no Satan and nothing evil throughout all the days of Joseph's life that he lived after his father Jacob.
And Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. He had lived in the land of Canaan for seventeen years and had lived as a slave for ten years.
And he made them swear an oath concerning his bones, because he knew that the Egyptians would not allow him to be taken out and buried in the land of Canaan at that time.

And he could not enter, because another, new king ruled over Egypt and was stronger than he was. He entered the land of Canaan, and the gates of Egypt were shut. No one went out, and no one entered Egypt.
And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the second year of the sixth week of years. They buried him in the land of Egypt, and all his brothers died after him.
And the king of Egypt went out to fight against the king of Canaan in the forty-seventh jubilee, in the second year of the second week of years.
And many returned to Egypt, while a few of them remained in the hill country of Hebron. Your father Abram remained with them.
And the king of Canaan defeated the king of Egypt and shut the gates of Egypt.
And the people of Egypt treated the children of Israel as unclean.
And she made a basket for you and coated it with pitch and bitumen. She placed it among the reeds at the riverbank and put you inside it for seven days.

And in the sixth year of the third week of years of the forty-ninth jubilee, you went and lived there for five weeks of years and one year. You returned to Egypt in the second year of the second week of years of the fiftieth jubilee.
And everything was sent [?] your hand, so that you would do what had not been done, and you were to tell it to the king of Egypt, before all his messengers and before his people.
And the Lord did everything for the sake of Israel.

Despite all the signs and wonders, Prince Mastema was not ashamed, until he grew strong and cried out to the Egyptians to pursue you with all their forces, with their chariots and horses, and with the entire multitude of the people of Egypt.
On the fourteenth, fifteenth, sixteenth, seventeenth, and eighteenth days, Prince Mastema was bound and shut away from the Israelites, so that he would not accuse them.

So that the Israelites would come and celebrate the Passover on its appointed day, the fourteenth day of the first month, between the evenings, from the third part of the day until the third part of the night; for two parts of the day were allotted to daylight, and the third to evening.

For great is the honor that the Lord gave Israel: to eat, drink, and be satisfied on this festival day, and to rest on it from all human work, except burning incense and bringing offerings and sacrifices before the Lord for the days and Sabbaths.
And anyone who does work, travels on a journey, or cultivates a field, whether at home or in any other place—
Anyone who does any of these things on the Sabbath day must die. Here ends the account of the Divisions of the Days.
